sentences: Here Jeong Seon compresses the whole of Mount Geumgang into a single round mass, as if seen from the sky.
No one could see this view from one spot; he wove together memories from several journeys to rebuild the mountain as a self-contained cosmos.
On the right, jagged rock peaks are drawn in sharp vertical strokes; on the left, the soft earthen hills are made of gentle ink dots.
The interlocking of hard and soft recalls the taegeuk, the union of yin and yang.
A poem praising the mountain is inscribed at the top, so text and image work as one.
It is at once a landscape and a map of a worldview.
